Subject: Private upgrade: fallback trigger & network evacuation protocol

Hi Sam / BrightBank team,

Thanks again for agreeing to the December maintenance window. Attached are the preflight checklist, the drain/evac script we plan to run, and a compact fallback decision matrix. High-level ask: please confirm that 02:00–05:00 UTC on Dec 16 works for your ops window and that your NetEng can accept BGP community changes during the drain (we use community 65535:100 to lower cost routes).

Key points we want to lock in before the window:
- Fallback triggers (immediate rollback criteria): CPU>85% sustained across control-plane nodes for 3 mins, >5% error-rate increase on NLB health checks for 2 consecutive minutes, or KV-cache miss storm impacting latency >2x.
- Network evacuation: we will withdraw the VIP and use graceful Envoy drain (conn drain 120s) then announce maintenance via a temporary AS-path prepend and the community noted above.
- Rollback path: snapshot restore + model-version pin to customer-stable (pinned v2026-11-09) with an automated canary check (5% traffic) for 10 minutes.

Attachments referenced here; please review the drain script and matrix before Thu Dec 14 so we can rehearse on your staging. If any of the above triggers are unacceptable, flag them now so we can adjust thresholds.

Karthik Iyer
Senior SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Karthik,

Thanks for the note. Dec 16 02:00–05:00 UTC is OK for us. NetEng can accept BGP community changes during the window but we need the exact AS-PATH prepend and community values to preconfigure filters (we lock changes to the edge 24h before).

A couple of clarifications from our side:
- What is the expected additional convergence time when you withdraw the VIP and apply the prepend? We need it for our monitoring and pager burn planning.
- For the KV-cache miss storm trigger, can you confirm how you measure the baseline? Is that percent increase relative to the 24h rolling median?

We'll review the attachments and get back with any redlines by EOD Thu.

—Sam

> - For the KV-cache miss storm trigger, can you confirm how you measure the baseline? Is that percent increase relative to the 24h rolling median?

Hi Sam — quick answers from the ops playbook: 
- Typical control-plane convergence after VIP withdrawal + BGP prepend is 45–90s to first successful failover, 2–4 minutes for full path reconvergence across our major peers depending on propagation. We account for this in the drain window and set Envoy conn drain to 120s to minimize loss.
- KV-cache miss baseline: we compute a 24h rolling median of miss-rate per capacity pool. The trigger is >200% of that median sustained for 3 mins. For BrightBank's config that maps to roughly 3x the normal miss count — we can run a separate preflight run on your staging and provide the exact numbers.

Operational notes we will enact during the window:
- Preflight: run synthetic traffic against staging for 30 mins to validate canary rollback path.
- Orchestration: our controller will attempt automated rollback on first trigger; if rollback fails, we will execute manual rollback with runbook step IDs (see attached matrix).
- Comms: Redwood will post step updates to the shared Ops channel and send state-change emails (start/finish/rollback) to the distribution list.

I'll coordinate a brief rehearsal on Dec 14 with your NetEng to validate BGP filters and keep a 60-minute rehearsal slot.

—Neha Kapoor
Sr. Manager, Private Deployments
